quests.instruction: On a building site, one worker checks that finished work follows the rules and is safe before the next stage can start. Who is it?
quests.hint: Think about the person who checks work before it moves on.
quests.explanation: Building inspectors check that work meets safety rules, so the next team can build on it with confidence.
quests.funFact: Inspectors often visit at different stages, because some parts are hidden once walls are finished.

quests.instruction: When astronauts work in space, a team on Earth watches data, answers questions, and helps solve problems. What is this team called?
quests.hint: Think about the team that stays in touch with the spacecraft.
quests.explanation: Mission control teams monitor a spaceflight, talk with the crew, and solve problems together with them.
quests.funFact: Mission control teams work in shifts so someone is always watching the mission.

quests.instruction: On a film set, who decides how each scene should look and guides the actors and the crew?
quests.hint: Think about the person with the main vision for the film.
quests.explanation: Directors guide the actors and crew so every part of the film works together to tell the story.
quests.funFact: A film can involve hundreds of people, from camera crews to costume makers.

quests.instruction: On a sports team, who helps injured players recover and return to play safely?
quests.hint: Think about the team member who looks after players' bodies.
quests.explanation: Sports physiotherapists treat injuries and plan exercises, so players can return to training safely with the coach's agreement.
quests.funFact: Many teams warm up with exercises designed to help prevent injuries.

quests.instruction: When a baby animal is born at the zoo, keepers care for it and the vet checks its health. Who explains the animal's story to visitors?
quests.hint: Think about the team member who teaches visitors.
quests.explanation: Zoo educators share facts and stories about animals, which helps visitors understand and care about wildlife.
quests.funFact: Zoos often run talks and feeding sessions where visitors can ask questions.

quests.instruction: Who leads an orchestra so that the musicians start, stop, and play together?
quests.hint: Think about the person at the front with a baton.
quests.explanation: Conductors set the speed and mood of the music and signal when each group of instruments should play.
quests.funFact: Conductors study the whole score, not just one instrument's part.

quests.instruction: At a port, who loads and unloads cargo from ships using cranes and trucks?
quests.hint: Think about the team that moves goods between ship and shore.
quests.explanation: Dock workers move cargo between ships and land, working with crane operators and truck drivers.
quests.funFact: Containers are stacked in standard sizes, so cranes can lift them easily.

quests.instruction: After a storm, who sends repair crews to the right streets using maps and reports?
quests.hint: Think about the person who decides where the crews go.
quests.explanation: Dispatchers collect reports, plan routes, and send the right crews to the right places.
quests.funFact: Dispatchers often use maps on screens to see where help is needed.

quests.instruction: Between flights, who inspects a plane's engines and parts to make sure it is safe to fly?
quests.hint: Think about the team that checks the plane itself.
quests.explanation: Aircraft technicians inspect, repair, and test planes so they are safe for the next flight.
quests.funFact: Aircraft parts have records so technicians know when each part was last checked.

quests.instruction: Why do plumbers and electricians often work after the walls are built but before the plaster is added?
options: They prefer to work in empty quiet rooms
Plaster is actually made from wires
They can put pipes and wires inside first
quests.correctAnswer: They can put pipes and wires inside first
quests.hint: Think about what is easier to hide once walls are finished.
quests.explanation: Pipes and wires are easier to fit before walls are covered, and the plasterer finishes the surface afterwards.
quests.funFact: Building teams plan the order of jobs so one team does not undo another team's work.

quests.instruction: In a restaurant, who greets guests, finds them a table, and tells the waiters where they are sitting?
quests.hint: Think about the first person guests meet.
quests.explanation: Hosts welcome guests and organize seating, which helps waiters and the kitchen plan their work.
quests.funFact: Hosts often keep a booking list so tables are ready when guests arrive.

quests.instruction: A doctor orders a scan. Who prepares the patient and operates the scanning machine?
quests.hint: Think about the specialist who takes pictures inside the body.
quests.explanation: Radiographers are trained to run imaging machines and take pictures that doctors use to understand a patient's health.
quests.funFact: Imaging machines need careful settings so that pictures are clear and safe.

quests.instruction: Which team could work together to rescue a hiker from a remote hillside?
quests.hint: Think about finding the hiker, getting to them, and giving care.
quests.explanation: A rescue may need people on the ground, a helicopter pilot for access, and a paramedic for medical care.
quests.funFact: Rescue teams plan carefully and keep in touch by radio.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best describes how an architect and a builder work together?
options: They never talk to each other about the plan
The builder designs; the architect lays bricks
They share ideas to turn a plan into a building
quests.correctAnswer: They share ideas to turn a plan into a building
quests.hint: Think about a plan becoming a real building.
quests.explanation: Architects design a building and builders make it real, and they talk to solve problems that appear along the way.
quests.funFact: Plans can change when builders find something unexpected on site.

quests.instruction: Dairy worker → ______ → shelf stacker. Who completes the chain that gets milk to the store shelf?
quests.hint: Think about who moves the milk from the farm to the shop.
quests.explanation: Delivery drivers carry milk in cold trucks from the farm to shops so it stays fresh until it reaches shelves.
quests.funFact: Cold trucks have cooling units to keep food at a safe temperature.

quests.instruction: A firefighter finds an injured person inside a building. What should they tell the ambulance crew?
options: What they ate for lunch earlier today
Where the person is and what is wrong
Nothing at all, to avoid confusion
quests.correctAnswer: Where the person is and what is wrong
quests.hint: Think about information that helps the medical team.
quests.explanation: Clear information helps paramedics prepare the right care and reach the patient quickly.
quests.funFact: Emergency crews use short, clear messages so there is no confusion.

quests.instruction: A student has asthma and may need an inhaler. Who at school should know so they can help?
options: Only the school bus company staff
Nobody, so that it stays a secret
quests.hint: Think about the adults who are with the student during the day.
quests.explanation: When the right adults know about a student's health needs, they can help quickly and safely.
quests.funFact: Schools often keep health plans so staff know how to help each student.

quests.instruction: At a big outdoor concert, which team members help keep the crowd safe?
quests.hint: Think about crowd guidance, medical help, and safety.
quests.explanation: Stewards guide crowds, paramedics care for anyone who is hurt, and security officers protect the venue.
quests.funFact: Large events usually have a safety plan that all these teams read in advance.

quests.instruction: A pilot has a small technical problem and needs advice from the ground. Who should the pilot talk to?
quests.hint: Think about the person who guides planes by radio.
quests.explanation: Air traffic controllers talk to pilots, give instructions, and arrange safe paths and landings.
quests.funFact: Controllers can clear a runway quickly if a plane needs to land.

quests.instruction: Plastic bottles are collected, sorted at a recycling center, then melted and shaped into new items. Who completes the chain after sorting?
quests.hint: Think about who turns sorted materials into new products.
quests.explanation: Factory workers use machines to turn recycled materials into new products, after sorters have separated them.
quests.funFact: Recycled plastic can be turned into things such as clothing fibers and park benches.

quests.instruction: Before opening night, who makes sure the costumes fit, are repaired, and are ready for each scene?
quests.hint: Think about the team member who looks after clothes for the show.
quests.explanation: Wardrobe assistants care for costumes, make small repairs, and help actors dress between scenes.
quests.funFact: Wardrobe teams often label each costume so quick changes go smoothly.

quests.instruction: Which skill is most helpful when working in a team?
quests.hint: Think about what helps people stay on the same page.
quests.explanation: Listening and sharing information help teams solve problems and avoid mistakes.
quests.funFact: Teams often hold short meetings to share updates.

quests.instruction: Two workers disagree about how to fix a machine. What is a good team approach?
options: Hear both ideas and test the safest
Ignore both ideas and flip a coin
Let the loudest voice always decide
quests.correctAnswer: Hear both ideas and test the safest
quests.hint: Think about being fair and safe.
quests.explanation: Good teams listen to different ideas and choose the safest, most reliable solution.
quests.funFact: Testing a fix on a small scale can help teams check it works before using it fully.

quests.instruction: The kitchen runs out of an ingredient before dinner. Who should the chef tell so the menu can change?
quests.hint: Think about who talks to the guests.
quests.explanation: If the kitchen shares changes, waiters can tell guests which dishes are unavailable and suggest alternatives.
quests.funFact: Many restaurants hold a short meeting before service so staff know what has changed.

quests.instruction: A flood damages a river bridge. Which order makes sense?
options: Engineer inspects, road workers close it, builders repair
Builders repair, engineer inspects, road workers close it
Road workers close it, builders repair, engineer inspects
quests.correctAnswer: Engineer inspects, road workers close it, builders repair
quests.hint: Think about checking and closing before repairing.
quests.explanation: An engineer checks the damage, the road is closed so people stay safe, and then builders repair the bridge.
quests.funFact: Bridges are closed whenever there is a danger, even if repairs take time.

quests.instruction: After a power failure at a hospital, which workers need to cooperate?
quests.hint: Think about power, patient care, and building systems.
quests.explanation: Electricians restore power, nurses keep caring for patients, and engineers check the building's systems.
quests.funFact: Hospitals plan for power failures, so everyone knows their role.

quests.instruction: Why do astronauts need engineers on Earth?
options: Engineers fly the spacecraft from home
Engineers choose only the astronauts' lunch
quests.hint: Think about problems that need many experts.
quests.explanation: Engineers on Earth study problems, test ideas, and send instructions to the crew in space.
quests.funFact: Engineers often test repair ideas on Earth before astronauts try them.

quests.instruction: Which statement best describes teamwork between professions?
options: Teams only work when everyone does the same task
Different workers share skills and information
Teams are only for very small jobs
quests.correctAnswer: Different workers share skills and information
quests.hint: Think about what the many teams in this course have in common.
quests.explanation: Teams use different skills and share information, so the whole job is done better than one person could manage alone.
quests.funFact: Even small tasks can involve several workers, such as a cook, a driver, and a shop assistant.

quests.instruction: Which group is most likely to work together to put on a school play?
options: Stage manager, lighting operator, costume maker
Airline pilot, village baker, and city judge
Welder, lifeguard, and underground coal miner
quests.correctAnswer: Stage manager, lighting operator, costume maker
quests.hint: Think about the backstage team.
quests.explanation: A stage manager keeps the show on time, a lighting operator controls lights, and a costume maker looks after the costumes.
quests.funFact: Backstage teams practice together so that changes in lights and costumes are smooth.

quests.instruction: A new playground opens. Which team helped make it possible?
options: Airline pilot, baker, judge, and miner
quests.hint: Think about planning, building, checking, and planting.
quests.explanation: A designer plans the playground, builders construct it, an inspector checks that it is safe, and gardeners care for the plants around it.
quests.funFact: Many places are open to the public only after safety checks are complete.
